analysis:
Examined SSDPrefixCache.swift head lines 1–1255 and the complete eviction patch. The supplied source excerpts are unchanged according to the complete range map. They preserve salted chain/HMAC lookup (533–542, 862–920), weight/layout metadata bindings (1057–1065), donation benefit and size gates (883–947), bounded write submission (1112–1125), and per-entry staging reservations with ticket-correlated adoption/release (204–246, 559–575, 630–650). Sliding-window writes use separate keyed tags and base commitments (1183–1185, 1220–1232). No new plaintext exposure, account-scope weakening, authorization change, or billing behavior is supported here; T-041's accepted timing residual is not a new finding.
The actual change at head 1772–1779 adds a closed-cache eviction guard and delegates victim selection/retirement to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest, retaining retireIndexedEntries as its deletion callback. This appears intended to prevent removal after teardown (close at 430–461), but the helper implementation and retirement synchronization are outside these units. Integration must verify that delegation preserves skipping undeletable victims, correct indexed-byte accounting, handling of external changes, and bounded progress under SSDDiskBudget enforcement. These are material to T-041's LRU/budget mitigation and provider availability (A-018), not evidence of an observed regression. Also reconcile closed-cache races against the helper's isClosed callback. No supported finding in this local scope; eviction safety remains unresolved pending that combined-source review.
